name: Regulatory Investigation / Subpoena
description: Regulatory inquiry response structure. Activates when a government regulator, agency, or enforcement authority issues a subpoena, CID (Civil Investigative Demand), formal inquiry, or announces an investigation. Legal-led response with strict document preservation obligations.
trigger_conditions: Subpoena or CID received from government agency (SEC, DOJ, FTC, CFPB, state AG, etc.)
Regulatory agency announces formal investigation into the organization
Search warrant executed at organization premises
Grand jury subpoena for documents or testimony
Regulatory information request that signals an enforcement investigation
Whistleblower complaint filed with regulator that triggers inquiry
Audit findings referred to enforcement division of regulator
Foreign regulator investigation (FCA, ESMA, CNIL, ICO, etc.)

crisis_lead.role: General Counsel (leads response; CEO is informed, not operational)
responsibilities: Overall command of legal response strategy
Direct internal investigation scope and priorities
Manage regulator relationships — single point of contact for regulator communications
Control information flow — lawyer-to-lawyer communications preferred
Assess legal exposure and develop defense strategy
Report to CEO and board on investigation status (privileged)
Decide when to engage external regulatory counsel

ops_lead.role: VP of Relevant Function (Compliance, Finance, Operations, etc.)
responsibilities: Coordinate document collection and data production under legal direction
Manage employee interviews and fact-gathering under privilege
Ensure business operations continue during investigation
Track investigation timeline and key deadlines (subpoena return dates)
Coordinate with IT on data preservation and e-discovery
Liaise with business teams to minimize disruption during document review
[GC] All external communications about investigation — single spokesperson is GC or designated external counsel
[GC] Liaise with SEC disclosure counsel for public company filing obligations (8-K, 10-Q contingency disclosures)
[GC] Manage press inquiries — typically 'we are cooperating fully with the investigation' only
[CMO] Internal communications to employees about the investigation
[CMO] Employee guidance on what to say/not say externally about the investigation
[CMO] Customer and partner talking points if investigation becomes public
Lead defense strategy and regulatory engagement
Prepare and manage document productions, privilege logs, and rolling productions
Conduct internal investigation interviews under Upjohn warnings
Prepare employees for testimony or depositions with regulator
Negotiate scope of investigation with regulator (narrowing, timing, burden)
Advise on self-disclosure obligations and cooperation credit
Manage parallel proceedings (civil, criminal, administrative)
Coordinate with criminal defense counsel if criminal exposure exists

key_actions: 1. PRESERVE ALL DOCUMENTS — Issue litigation hold immediately. No document destruction under any circumstances. Destruction of documents = obstruction of justice (criminal offense, separate from underlying violation)
2. Designate single point of contact for all regulator communications — no one else speaks to the regulator without explicit authorization from General Counsel
3. Engage external regulatory counsel immediately — specialist firm with regulator-specific experience (SEC, DOJ, FTC, etc.)
4. Legal hold notice to all employees and IT — preserve all relevant documents, emails, Slack messages, Teams chats, and electronic records. Suspend auto-deletion policies and recycling of backups
5. Prepare data room for document production — e-discovery platform, collection protocols, review team, production format specifications
6. Employee interview preparation — Upjohn warnings before any internal interviews. Employees should understand they are represented by company counsel, not individually represented
7. Privilege log planning — identify all potentially privileged documents, track claimed privilege basis, be prepared to defend privilege claims if challenged
8. Assess self-disclosure or cooperation strategy — investigate whether voluntary disclosure or cooperation credit is available under applicable regulatory framework
9. Parallel proceedings assessment — identify any simultaneous civil litigation, criminal investigation, or other regulatory proceedings that create risk or strategy implications
10. SEC disclosure assessment (if public) — evaluate 8-K filing obligation, 10-Q/10-K disclosure requirements for material investigations, risk factor updates
11. Employee communication and training — do not discuss investigation externally. No social media posts. No discussions with former employees who may be contacted by regulator
12. Board notification and reporting — privileged update to board within 72 hours. Ongoing privileged reporting throughout investigation

communication_protocol.internal: Strict need-to-know. General Counsel controls all information flow. Legal hold notice sent to affected departments. No discussion of investigation details in unsecured channels. No internal discussion of investigation strategy on email or Slack (privilege risk). Employees directed to refer any regulator inquiries to General Counsel immediately.
communication_protocol.external: Single external spokesperson: General Counsel or designated external counsel. Standard response: 'We are cooperating fully with the investigation and cannot comment further on an ongoing matter.' No public discussion of facts, legal strategy, or investigation status. No press interviews. No analyst briefings about the investigation.
communication_protocol.cadence: GC leads daily internal standup during active investigation phases. Weekly privileged reporting to CEO. Monthly privileged reporting to board (or more frequently if material). Document production deadlines driven by subpoena/CID return dates.

escalation_timeline.t0_24hr: Receive subpoena/CID/inquiry notification → Engage external counsel → Issue legal hold → Designate SPOC for regulator → Brief CEO
escalation_timeline.t24_72hr: Internal investigation kickoff → Data collection begins → Employee Upjohn interviews → Board notification (privileged) → Preliminary exposure assessment
escalation_timeline.t1_2wk: Document collection and review → Privilege log preparation → Regulator kickoff meeting (if appropriate) → Initial production or response deadline
escalation_timeline.t2_8wk: Rolling document productions → Employee testimony preparation → Factual investigation continues → Defense strategy refinement → Settlement evaluation (if applicable)
escalation_timeline.t2_6mo: Ongoing productions → Regulatory meetings and presentations → Privilege log challenges → Parallel proceedings coordination → Resolution negotiations or litigation preparation
